svg.title: Arm D flow
svg.text: Arm D — a diffusion prior on clean crops, conditioned on one frame
Top: how the prior is trained (never a noisy frame). Bottom: how one measured frame is turned into a sample.
prior training — 40 000 steps on 64-px crops of the 76 TRAIN clean images (flips on)
loss ‖ ε_θ(√ᾱ_t x + √(1−ᾱ_t) ε, t) − ε ‖²
standard DDPM; unconditional samples carry grain, vias, blemishes
inference — SDEdit-style chain: the frame IS the state of the chain at its own noise level
t* ≈ 115 is the level whose noise matches the frame's variance (0.16)
25 DDIM steps, η = 1 (fresh noise each step); each step: predict x̂₀, re-noise to the next level
No likelihood term at all — the frame enters only as the start state.
The exact-likelihood chain (`dps`, proximal Poisson step per iteration)
is documented in §6: stable, but 25–28 dB with this prior.
What it buys: PSNR ≈ N2N, bias at the oracle's level (the prior never saw clipped frames), synthetic grain texture. What it costs: +41 % pixel σ and +0.2 px CD 3σ as a single sample,
and LESS blemish contrast than arm A (0.60 vs 0.68): the chain re-samples what the frame does not pin down instead of measuring it. A display channel, not a metrology estimator.
